title: Quirk portfolio and sprint hooks synthesis
body:
Purpose and quick context:
This note collects smaller, recurring runtime/user-quirks reported by customers over Q3–Q4 2026 and turns them into a compact "patch portfolio" we can slot into upcoming sprints. Intended for engineering triage + PM prioritization. Many items are low-effort UX/ops fixes; a few are medium-risk perf or routing changes that need SRE review.

What I listened for (sources):
- Direct CS tickets (top 40 by frequency) July–September 2026
- 6 post-mortems where customer apps observed regression after model swap
- 3 field calls (large SaaS integration partners) + submitted logs
- Slack threads: #cs-runtime-{tickets} and #eng-serving-runtime

Top clusters (short descriptions + severity)
1) KV-cache warm-up failures (freq: high, sev: medium)
   - Symptoms: first few tokens much slower; cold-start prefix not cached across dedicated lanes; repeated customer steam: "their session jumps to 6s then back to 40ms"
   - Customer impact: interactivity apps (chat bots) see user churn on first reply
   - Root hypotheses: cache invalidation on rollouts + route mismatch on pinned versions
   - Quick mitigation ideas (1–2 sprint hooks): add a short-lived prewarm API call; expose cache-warm telemetry to customers; ticket: JIRA-INF-1127

2) Latency tail on short sequences (freq: medium, sev: high for PLG customers)
   - Symptoms: 95–99p latency spikes on <32-token calls during high concurrency
   - Cause signals: batching heuristics jump threshold; kernel selection path causing context setup overhead
   - Proposed patch: adjust small-request batching window and force fast-path kernel for sequences <64 when on dedicated; add experiment flag to enable/disable per-customer

3) Model variant fallback confusion (freq: medium, sev: low)
   - Customers reported surprising fallback to lower-quality variants during regional capacity shortage. Messaging to caller is opaque -> app-level correctness bugs.
   - UX patch: return structured "fallback_reason" in response; add a new console banner for active fallback rules. Low dev cost, high clarity ROI.

4) Embedding mismatch & versioning (freq: low, sev: medium)
   - Issue: embeddings dimension drift when models updated; clients didn't pin vector schema -> retrieval mismatches
   - Action: add schema header in embedding response (model+dim+embed-hash); generate a one-click migration note in Console when rolling embedding-incompatible versions.

Micro patches (fast wins - 1 sprint each)
- Expose per-request route_id in logs visible in Console trace view (PR: small changeset)
- Add quickstart snippet showing recommended cache-prewarm pattern for chat apps
- Add "fallback_reason" field to generation response (as above)
- Provide explicit error text when quantized model fails negotiation in Private installs

Medium effort (2–4 sprints)
- Small-request fast-path kernel experiment + telemetry
- Console: rollout map showing active model variants by region with historical duration
- Dedicated pool policy: allow "reserve-warm" instances for top-tier customers (ops + billing implication)

Cost / risk notes
- Reserve-warm instances increase committed cost; propose experiment with 10 pilot customers to reimburse via credits
- Fast-path kernel changes require careful perf regression tests across sequence lengths and quantization profiles; schedule perf lab window and synthetic tests

Customer quotes (verbatim-ish)
- "We lose users on first reply; warm-up is killing our demo conversions." — eng from fintech-app A
- "Our reranking accuracy dropped after your model swap; we had to roll back to keep production stable." — search product lead B

Next steps (recommended immediate actions)
1) PM + Eng sync: prioritize micro patches into next weekly sprint; own: Marcus Chen
2) Schedule perf lab window to run fast-path kernel experiments; owner: eng-serving-runtime
3) CS to run targeted outreach to top 12 impacted customers offering prewarm credits and gather more logs; owner: Aisha Patel
4) Design: create console mock for fallback visibility (linked: CONFLUENCE-5234)

Open questions / data we need
- Exact frequency of KV-cache cold starts by customer tier (CS to extract top 50)
- Does dedicated routing ever map to wrong model variant when pinning is enabled? (SRE tracing)
- Cost delta estimate for reserve-warm instances per GPU-week (Finance + Infra)

Notes to self / TODOs
- Draft short CS playbook "If customer reports slow first token" (templated reply + log gathering steps)
- Follow up on PR #46 for kv-cache telemetry; check failing tests

Attachment pointers
- Logs: attached to JIRA-INF-1127 and customer gist links in the ticket
- Design mock: CONFLUENCE-5234

Summary (one-liner):
A compact portfolio of small-to-medium fixes (cache prewarm, fallback visibility, small-request fast-path) that together eliminate the most frequent customer friction points impacting conversions and perceived reliability. Many are high-clarity, low-effort wins we should pipeline immediately.

-- Aisha
